free_tier.stated: The model VS2-free can be used free of charge in the basic version with IPv6 and is ideal for testing, as a development environment or as the basis for creating larger and growing systems.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a tunnel or an address, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a live tunnel, not stored bytes

egress.terms: Traffic | monthly included traffic volume | 1 TB; ingress: udp
egress.free_allowance: Traffic | monthly included traffic volume | 1 TB

interface_detail: full root over SSH, reached at the container's IPv6 /128
tooling: wg-quick if the container exposes /dev/net/tun, otherwise a userspace fallback such as wireguard-go over a TUN the container must still provide
chaining: 1 TB monthly transfer over IPv6 without a payment card composes as a secondary relay or regional endpoint.

limits.value: beyond the included volume the connection is capped to 1 Mbit/s

binding_note: 1 TB a month is 33.3 GB a day, 0.909 TiB, which is 9% short of 1 TiB if the vendor's TB is decimal, so the quota is the first wall and it fails by a narrow margin; the 1 Mbit/s cap behind it is the second wall, and 1 Mbit/s sustained is 10.8 GB a day, a third of even the included volume

identity_cost.detail: Contract terms specify manual renewal with no payment instrument required for free orders. Account registration requires contact details and postal address verification.

reliability_note: the contract renewal type is manual, so an unrenewed server lapses; traffic past 1 TB is capped to 1 Mbit/s rather than billed
confidence_note: the free-of-charge sentence, the 1 TB line, the 1 Mbit/s cap and the container virtualization type are all on the vendor page read today; whether 1 TB means decimal or binary, and whether the container has TUN, would both need a signup

evidence.proved: 'The model VS2-free can be used free of charge in the basic version with IPv6'
'Traffic | monthly included traffic volume | 1 TB' and 'If the inclusive traffic is exceeded, the connection becomes capped to 1Mbit/s, if no additional traffic is purchased by customer.'
'Virtualization Type | Linux Container', '1 Core @ 1 GHz', 'RAM | 1 GB', 'Harddisk | 10 GB HDD @ Raid10', '1x 1 GBit/s'
the IPv4 row reads 'IPv4-Addresses | free of charge | -' with 'additional IPv4 | EUR per IP / mo | yes, optional up to 16', and IPv6 is '1x /128', so the free unit is reachable over IPv6 only

notes: Free LXC container with 1 GHz CPU, 1 GB RAM, and 1 TB monthly IPv6 traffic. Container environment lacks /dev/net/tun by default, restricting kernel WireGuard deployment. Third-party accounts describe manual monthly renewals.

extras.wg_detail: the offer is 'Virtualization Type | Linux Container' with full root, so wg-quick installs; WireGuard needs /dev/net/tun and the page does not say whether the container exposes it, and an LXC container without TUN cannot load the module. Not tested, because signing up was out of budget for this lane
extras.volume_stated: Traffic | monthly included traffic volume | 1 TB
extras.transit_note: bytes leave through the host's 1 Gbit/s uplink, shared with the other containers on that host
